questions: Does the game end immediately when S becomes {1,2,...,N} (as per clarification) or after the player's turn completes? The clarification says 'right after the operation that completes it', but does 'right after' mean before the opponent gets a turn, i.e., the player who made S complete wins?

Is the set S initially empty, and does the game end when S becomes {1,2,...,N}? The clarification confirms this, but is there any other condition (like all A_i becoming zero) that could end the game earlier?
When a player chooses an index i, must A_i be positive at the start of their turn, or can they choose an i with A_i > 0 even if it's already in S?
If a player subtracts 1 from A_i and i is already in S, does the game check if S is complete before the next player's turn, or only if i was not in S before?
Are players allowed to choose the same index multiple times in a row, or is there any restriction on consecutive moves?
Does 'play optimally to win' imply they maximize their chance of winning given perfect play, and if a win is impossible, they try to draw? But since the game always ends, is a draw possible?
Is the input sequence A guaranteed to be of length N exactly, and are there any constraints on the sum of A_i or parity that might affect the outcome?
If S becomes complete during a player's operation, does that player win immediately, or does the game end after the operation with no explicit winner assignment in the rule?
